asr_transcript: Leopard seals are ambush hunters that feed in the water, not on land.  Now, say, you're the penguin.  The seal catches the penguin in the water, then brings its prey to the surface to feed.  The best place for this is the ice edge, where penguins bunch up before they dive.  In one study at Prids Bay, seals worked the fast ice edge where departing Adelie penguins  gathered.  Researchers saw five different hunting techniques, and estimated that just six seals could eat  about 2.7% of the adult Adelie population over roughly 120 days.  Now look at who else stands at the ice edge.  Penguins stand upright.  So do you.  The researcher's best idea is that against white ice, you look like a dark, upright shape,  and the only other thing that stands up out there is a penguin.
